topic: Mastering Derivatives: Geometric Intuition and Essential Formulas
target_audience: High school students or introductory college calculus students

sections.title: The Foundation: Prerequisite - What is a Slope?
lecture_lines: Imagine a blue plank on a coordinate grid.
Turbo moves along the line from start to finish.
A triangle shows he rises two for every one.
This constant rate of change is the slope, two.
But what happens if the path is a curve?
animations: Display a coordinate grid with a blue (#0000FF) line y=2x.
Move a small snail icon 'Turbo' along the line segment from (0,0) to (1,2).
Draw a red (#FF0000) right triangle highlighting 'Rise=2' and 'Run=1'.
Show the text 'Slope = 2' in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the triangle.
Morph the line into a white parabola and mark a point with a blinking green (#00FF00) dot.

sections.title: The Geometric Intuition: Local Linearity
lecture_lines: Look at this point on a curved rollercoaster track.
A tangent line touches the curve at this spot.
Let's zoom in closely on this specific point.
Up close, the curve looks like a straight line.
This local linearity defines the derivative's value here.
animations: Draw a white parabola y = x^2 and mark point P at (1,1).
Add a golden (#FFD700) tangent line at point P.
Perform a camera zoom-in centered on point P by a factor of 20.
The parabola segment within the zoom becomes indistinguishable from the tangent line.
Add the label 'Local Linearity' in white text next to the point.

sections.title: The Power Rule: The Geometry of Growing Squares
lecture_lines: Imagine a square with side x and area x-squared.
As x grows, thin strips appear on the edges.
A tiny corner piece also forms as it expands.
The two side strips each have an area of x.
The Power Rule proves this growth rate is 2x.
animations: Draw a white square with side 'x'. Label the area 'x^2' in the center.
Animate two light blue (#ADD8E6) strips appearing on the right and top edges.
Highlight the corner where the strips meet with a small red (#FF0000) square of area 'dx^2'.
Indicate that the two main strips each have area 'x * dx'.
Show the text 'Total Growth ≈ 2x * dx' in yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Trigonometric Derivatives: The Rhythm of the Circle
lecture_lines: A rider travels around this circular Ferris wheel.
Their vertical position follows a smooth sine wave.
Their vertical speed matches the circle's horizontal cosine.
animations: Show a white unit circle with a radius rotating at constant angular velocity.
Trace the vertical height (sine value) as a green (#00FF00) vertical line.
Draw a horizontal vector representing the rate of change, identifying it as cosine.

sections.title: Summary: The Speedometer of Change
lecture_lines: Formulas provide shortcuts for finding local steepness.
The speedometer shows how fast the curve changes.
You now have the intuition to master calculus!
animations: Simultaneously draw a white curve on the left and a speedometer on the right.
The speedometer needle (#FF4500) rotates based on the curve's current slope.
Flash the text 'Derivative = Speed of Change' in white across the center.
